citations.narrative:
The facility does not have an accurate record of all regulated animals present on the premises. The records are missing
approximately 805 animals that were located in a second building not previously disclosed to APHIS officials. Additionally,
the facility does not have a record of animals that have been acquired in this second undisclosed building.
Improper recordkeeping does not allow APHIS officials to properly account for animals on the premises or allow for proper
tracking of animals. Each dealer and exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly
disclose all information required by the AWA concerning each animal purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, or
otherwise in his or her possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, euthanized, sold, or otherwise
disposed of by that dealer or exhibitor.

Multiple enclosures in the second animal housing building have sharp points that are accessible to the animals. There is
rust and corrosion creating sharp points and jagged edges on dust baths, enclosure fronts, food and water receptacles.
Failure to ensure that the enclosures are maintained in good repair can result in injury to the animals and decreased
structural strength.
Correct by ensuring that the facility is constructed of such material and such strength as appropriate for the animals
involved. The indoor and outdoor housing facility shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to
protect the animals from injury and to contain the animals.

A strong odor of ammonia is present in the second building animal housing area. The inspectors' eyes felt irritated
throughout the inspection of the building. The licensee stated that cleaning in the building has ranged in cleaning from one
to two weeks.
High levels of ammonia can cause discomfort to the animals and lead to further health issues.
Indoor housing facilities shall be adequately ventilated by natural or mechanical means to provide for the health and to
prevent discomfort of the animals at all times. Such facilities shall be provided with fresh air either by means of windows,
doors, vents, fans, or air-conditioning and shall be ventilated so as to minimize drafts, odors, and moisture condensation.
The licensee must ensure that the ammonia is kept at a compliant level either by removal of ammonia causing waste
and/or proper ventilation at all times in order to support the health of the animals.

The facility is not adequately cleaning the premises. In the second building housing area that houses approximately 805
chinchillas, there is an excess of discarded bedding and fecal material on the floors between the rows of animal
enclosures. There are excessive amounts cobwebs observed throughout the facility in both buildings including on top of
and behind the enclosures currently housing approximately 1147 animals. Multiple enclosures were observed with clumps
of hair from the animals trapped in the wire fencing in both the front and rear of the enclosures. Hair was also seen caught
on the automatic watering lines. Unused enclosures and runs that attach multiple enclosures for breeding contain multiple
cobwebs trapping debris. Additionally, spaces in this building not currently being used to house animals are cluttered with
accumulation of trash, dust, debris, soiled animal bedding, cobwebs, equipment, and miscellaneous items.
Failure to adequately clean the animal enclosures and the premises can lead to illness, transmission of diseases, and
attract unwanted pests. The facility must ensure that the premises are kept clean and in good repair to protect the animals
from injury to facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.

A safe pest control method is not being utilized at the facility. The facility had multiple empty enclosures with open packets
of rat poison among enclosures currently housing animals. These enclosures were present in a second previously
undisclosed building of the facility. Inspectors observed one enclosure with open rat poison that is directly adjacent to
enclosures currently housing chinchillas on the sides and above/below the open bait.
Failure to ensure that rodent poison is used at a safe distance from other rodents (chinchillas) risks accidental poisoning
of the covered species and is a threat to animal welfare.
A safe and effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests shall be
established and maintained. Correct by, 06-August-2026.

There is an insufficient number of adequately trained employees to carry out the level of husbandry practices and care
required by the Animal Welfare Act. There is only two full-time people responsible for the care of approximately 1147
animals at this facility. There is a history of numerous non-compliances identified pertaining to the cleaning, sanitation,
watering, and veterinary care.
The issues seen are consistent with shortages of personnel. Insufficient personnel can lead to a failure in maintenance of
the facility, delayed care for the animals, and unnecessary suffering and health concerns for the animals. The facility must
ensure a sufficient number of adequately trained employees are utilized to maintain the professionally acceptable level of
husbandry practices set forth in this subpart. Such practices shall be under the supervision of an animal caretaker who
has a background in animal husbandry or care. Correct by, 14-August-2026.
This is a continuation of the report for the routine inspection conducted 05-August-2026 and contains the remaining non-
compliances found during the inspection. The exit briefing for the items included on this report was conducted on 06-
August-2026.
Additional Inspectors:
Eric Irvin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
